reason: AC1-AC14 are the acceptance gate; AC2, AC5, AC7, AC8, and AC11 are the security-critical ones
Load-bearing decisions to verify: no metadata columns, no separate test endpoint, v1. envelope with a cached scrypt key, owner filter in WHERE, provenance derived not stored
Authorization tests are mandatory; AC2 and AC8 must be verified by reading the service, not the UI
Verify snake_case plural naming, UUIDv7 text ids, timestamptz, and that 0003 applies from an empty database. Do NOT flag the absent catalog metadata columns — PRD P1 sanctions that deviation
Verify a failed ownership filter returns NOT_FOUND rather than FORBIDDEN, and that no upstream provider body reaches a response
Verify no plaintext key, envelope, or Authorization header reaches a log line
Verify no service signature mentions NextRequest/NextResponse, no query sits in a Route Handler, and no db import escapes src/server/
Verify provider configs and the available-model list live in TanStack Query and are not mirrored into Zustand or a client-side role check
Verify a11y on the provider forms, "use client" placement, and that only the rule-encoding share-toggle branch is unit tested
Discovery and model add/remove cross transport, service, adapter, and UI; check the contract holds end to end
Step 10 is an explicit ponytail pass; the OwnConfig/SharedConfig mappers and any one-call Drizzle wrappers are the likely cuts
